restrictions: The two messages have 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 bytes for one t with 1 <= t < 2^32: t zero chunks of 1024 bytes followed by a last chunk of one block. The last chunk is compressed as a non-root chunk with counter t (v12 = t, v13 = 0), flags 3 and its true block length; the 63-byte block ends in eight zero bytes, so words 14 and 15 and the top byte of word 13 are zero in both zero-filled blocks. Equal last-chunk chaining values give equal digests by the tree lemma of proof.md Section 7.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.

Exact part: for every trial of proof.md Section 8 the two last-chunk chaining values agree on words 0, 2, 5 and 7, E1.c1 lies in the cube of beta* = 18b0e098 so that beta = beta* in every trial, Y4 ranges over the whole class of eta (524,288 values; no sub-class, no rule on h1), and the counter t is solved per trial as ROL(K0.d1,16) XOR K0.a1; trials with t = 0 are skipped. Only outer steps that pass the exact filter of Section 8 for S = {175,185,275,285,385,685}020a0 (share 2^-9.9782) and that the exact s-pattern pre-check keeps reach the solver. It follows the one path of the static slot named by five fresh selector bits of the step's word (proof.md 9.8) and certifies at most one trial: each listed success of a step owns exactly one of 32 slots (Lemmas F, VP, G7, SL), so a step certifies one with probability exactly N/32. Heuristic part: 2^95.460 walked trials (2^74.460 outer steps of 2^21) give a collision with probability at least 0.39 under H1' and H4'.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5, 430 machine units (operations, loads, stores) per unit, on a 64-register load/store machine with immediate constants; each fetch of a memory word costs one load. Outer steps run seven to a batch in lean packed 36-bit lanes: 425 units per batch (the raw eighth word kept for the selector), 35 per lane whose test-(2) mask meets S (its Q path), 512 per passing lane (rebuild and 16-unit pre-check included), and 8,912 for the slot selection, the one-path solver of proof.md 9.8 with the guard (G7) and the certificate of its root when the pre-check keeps the step: proved upper allowances of a specified layout, not measured or implemented counts. No sorting, no lookup by value, no table that grows with the trials. The run halts with failure when the test-(2), pass or solver count exceeds its budget, or after RUN_BATCHES batches; each row is charged at its budget plus one, and no mean of a work count is used (proof.md Section 11).

Randomized by eight fresh uniform 256-bit words per batch of seven outer steps; each outer step reads its own disjoint bits, its selector from bits 0, 1, 8, 9 and 15 of its eighth word, which the member does not read (Lemma PL). Success 0.39 holds only under H1' (a mean rate, no dependence clause), H4' (three budget clauses for this run) and HSEL (the return of SEL). The factor 98,937,639,497 in H1' is five sevenths of the model count of S on the class, rounded down, and is not measured by the organizer-run experiments, which run the root instance (counter 0, flags 11): no digest experiment can show a half-collision of a non-root chunk. Filter, pre-check, (G7) and slots are exact. No full 2-round collision is exhibited. The submitted program runs this search with the slot of proof.md 9.8 on the root instance only, where a root is a collision only if its forced counter word is 0, and counts by the ledger of Section 11; its run length and budgets are those of entry 0bc5f130, never reached in a trial.

Six 32-bit constants, the word eta, the beta* cube (beta*, mask, value), the seven tau values and eps of the filter's automata and the mask of S are what the search reads (73 bytes); the submitted program stores no sub-class or rule-A words. The constants were found by a participant's solver search and chosen by one exact count per model; beta* is the beta of that solution, and S has the least exact charge of the complete traversal among the 16,383 nonempty outcome sets. preprocessing_log2 55 bounds the selection procedure SEL of proof.md Section 12 (below 2^62.946 operations) in full and is included in time_log2: the search alone is below 2^71.74802 units, SEL below 2^54.198. That SEL returns these values rests on records and a stated, unproved operation-rate bridge (heuristic HSEL). memory_log2_bytes 44 covers the two output messages (each below 2^42 bytes), the code, SEL and the search, all held at once. No priority or novelty claim is made.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical; a mean rate only. Over the run's RUN_STEPS independent uniform 256-bit words, let N_o be the number of listed good valid trials of one outer step (t != 0, R = 0, and an E1 outcome in S = {175,185,275,285,385,685}020a0, six outcomes of beta*; Y4 in the whole class of eta; no rule on h1), counted over all of Q* whether or not the outer step passes the filter or the pre-check. Rate: E[N_o] >= (2^21 - 1) q with q = FACTOR * 2^-128, FACTOR = floor(5 * 138,512,695,296 / 7) = 98,937,639,497, about 2^-91.474 (just under five sevenths of the conditional model rate p of Lemma S1 for S). Nothing else is assumed about N_o: no clause on how the listed good trials of one outer step depend on each other and no bound on its factorial ratio rho. The search certifies at most one trial per outer step, the one of the static slot named by five fresh selector bits, and every listed good trial of a step owns exactly one of 32 slots, so the certified count N_32 is 0 or 1 with E[N_32] = E[N_o] / 32 exactly, whatever the joint law of the trials (Lemma SL, GPT Sol answer BA 1.3); with RUN_STEPS = ceil(0.49512 * 32 * 2^128 / (FACTOR (2^21 - 1))) the run fails to certify a trial with probability at most exp(-0.49512) (proof.md 10.4). This is the rate clause of entry 26ebba63, restated for the whole class and S; that entry's clause, reviewed (plausible_not_refuted), was for the sub-class of 2^17 members with rule A and seven outcomes and does not by itself imply this law (GPT Sol, answer AT 2), so it is declared here anew. Entry 0bc5f130 declared this rate together with a dependence clause (rho <= 0.0065 sufficient); that clause is dropped. By Lemma F every listed good trial lies in an outer step that passes the filter, and by Lemmas VP and G7 the pre-check and the guard (G7) skip none, so N_o is the same count, pointwise (GPT Sol, answers AW 1 and AX 1.2).
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Sections 8 and 9: lengths 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 with a non-root last chunk (counter t, v13 = 0, flags 3), the six constants of Section 3.2, Y4 a member of the whole class of eta (524,288 values, Lemma Q) drawn with the outer words from the run's fresh 256-bit words (seven outer steps to a batch, each on its own disjoint bits, Lemma PL), E1.c1 drawn from the cube of beta* = 18b0e098 in every trial, t solved per trial and t = 0 skipped. N_o counts all of Q* in every outer step and only the six outcomes of S; the clause concerns its mean only. The selector bits, the slots and the one-path solver (proof.md 9.8) do not change N_o.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the participant's exact count, in integer arithmetic under the seven-word model of Section 10 with Y4 uniform in the class, of the part of beta* on the class carried by the six outcomes of S (67,633,152 = 1,032 * 2^16 on the per-trial scale 2^-83 of the class; the counting program and the six rows of its output are printed in Section 17), times 2^11 for drawing E1.c1 from the cube (Lemma S1), taken at five sevenths, rounded down. The filter, the pre-check and (G7) change neither the count nor the premise (Lemmas S9 (b), VP and G7), and the slots keep exactly 1/32 of the mean (Lemma SL), which the run length pays. Participant evidence of Section 13, untrusted by the harness: a whole-class graphics-card run of 2^46 real counter trials in 2^25 passing outer steps, with a sub-class control of the same size, in which every measured quantity matches the exact model within 1.5 clustered standard errors, among them the E1 rate on the whole class of the seven outcomes of entry 59f8915e, 1.0020 +- 0.0086 of the model (13,595 events), and its ratio to the sub-class rate, 0.9895 +- 0.0120 (model 1); that counter covered the seven together, so the E1 event of S is a sub-event of the measured event (52/53 of it in the model) and was not counted on its own; 2^43 real trials inside passing outer steps of the seven-outcome filter on the sub-class, listed E1 outcome 0.979 +- 0.022 of its value; and a reduced-width (8-bit) end-to-end run of complete messages, with no sub-class and no rule, in which the counter arrangement found 251 collisions against 255.0 predicted. The joint 128-bit event itself, about 2^-91 per trial, is not measured at 32 bits.
heuristics.limitations: The factor 98,937,639,497 is assumed (five sevenths of the model count of the six outcomes of S on the class, rounded down). The premise of entry 26ebba63, reviewed (plausible_not_refuted), was for the sub-class with rule A; it is not inherited, and the whole-class mean of N_o for S is declared, not proved. The organizer-run experiments run the root instance (counter 0, flags 11) of the same construction and measure neither the factor nor the counter half-collision, which no digest experiment can show. The transfer of the single-trial law to the actual sampler is partly proved (Lemmas S1-S5, S9, VP, G7) and partly assumed; how much of the success mass the member with t = 0 carries is not proved. The whole-class graphics-card run measures the E1 side of the seven outcomes together and the filter, not the six of S on their own, not the E3 side (N3 four times that of the sub-class) nor the joint event. Lemma SL needs (PHASE) and (P*) for every joint root; the verifier of proof.md 9.9 certifies both in all eight phases and was run by the participant, not by the organizer. The slot selection, the one-path solver and its cap of 8,912 are proved allowances; the submitted program runs their logic on the root instance only, with ledger counts, not the 64-register schedule, and has found no root that reached the test t = 0. The price of dropping the dependence clause is a run about 32 times as long.

heuristics.statement: Supporting. Three count-budget clauses for the run of this package, with one failure allowance for their union: with probability at least 0.9995 over the coins all three hold, so no budget halts the run. (a) Pass budget: at most PASS_BUDGET = 27,372,319,633,926,710,491 outer steps pass the filter for S (nominal share pi = 279,070,422,111 / 2^48 = 2^-9.9782). (b) Pre-check budget: at most SOLVER_BUDGET = 6,843,079,908,481,677,623 outer steps have a nonzero T = X AND VMASK[nu] and reach the solver (nominal share 558,140,844,222 / 2^51 = pi / 4, exact in the counting model with nu uniform and independent; a physical clause, not a consequence of (a)). (c) Lean test-(2) budget: at most E_BUDGET = 1,502,329,371,444,650,570,489 lanes have a test-(2) mask meeting S and run the Q path (nominal share 233,715,456 / 2^32 = 2^-4.1998). Each budget is ceil(17/16 * RUN_STEPS * share) with RUN_STEPS = 25,984,157,895,075,365,790,188. These are the clauses of entry 0bc5f130 stated for this run, about 32 times longer: a tail bound for a run of fixed length does not by itself extend to a longer one (GPT Sol, answer BA 1.4). Reaching a budget halts with failure; the time bound charges each budget plus one. The guard (G7) and the selector add no clause: the solver count is taken before either runs.
heuristics.scope: The counts N_E, N_2 and N_3 of proof.md 10.3 over the RUN_STEPS outer steps of step 1 of Section 9.1, with Y4 drawn from the whole class: each is binomial over independent outer steps (Lemma PL) with the sampler's probability of its indicator; the three indicators of one outer step may depend on each other in any way, and none depends on the selector.
heuristics.extrapolation: The nominal shares are exact for uniform independent (Y9, omega) and, for (b), an independent uniform three-bit nu (GPT Sol, answers AC, AN and AW 3; the certificate of Section 8). If each sampler probability is at most 1.06 times its nominal share, the Chernoff bound puts each overflow below exp(-RUN_STEPS * share * 53 / 18,020,000): exp(-4.1 * 10^15), exp(-7.5 * 10^13) and exp(-1.8 * 10^13), so their union is below 3 * exp(-1.8 * 10^13), far below 0.0005, without independence inside an outer step (GPT Sol, answers AW 3 and BA 1.4). Measured (Section 13, untrusted by the harness, Python's generator, whole class): on 60,000,000 real outer steps the three counts are 1.0004 +- 0.0005 (test (2)), 0.9980 +- 0.0041 (pass) and 1.0123 +- 0.0082 (pre-check) of their nominal values; on another 30,000,000 the pass count is 0.9981 +- 0.0058 of its nominal value and the share of passing steps that survive the pre-check is 0.25101 against 1/4; over both runs that share is 0.2527 +- 0.0015. The bit identity behind the pre-check held on 324,098 of 324,098 real trials.
heuristics.limitations: That each sampler probability is at most 1.06 times its nominal share is not proved: the sampler's Y9, omega and nu are not proved independent and uniform, and the quarter share of the pre-check is a share of a model with nu uniform, not a property of the sampler. The measurements are two runs of one generator made after the design, not a locked validation, and far shorter than this run. The time bound, the filter, the pre-check, (G7) and the slots do not depend on these shares.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical; the return of the selection procedure only. The selection procedure SEL of proof.md Section 12, run as written there, returns the values that the search reads as advice (73 bytes, nonuniform_advice_log2_bytes 7): the six constants X3 = 29d4fa98, X7 = bee3af28, X11 = 44036000, X15 = 40c58500, W4 = 97475638 and W13 = 0007c006 of proof.md 3.2 (step 1: the 116 runs of the participant's solver log with their logged seeds, each capped at 2^56 operations); eta = 830303cf and beta* = 18b0e098, the class and the beta of the model with the largest part (step 2: one integer count per model, capped at 2^52, ties broken by the order of the log); and, by the fixed rule of step 3, the cube of beta* (mask 0e09818b, value 02008000), its outcomes on the class with the seven values of tau and eps of the filter's automata, and S = 5f, the six outcomes {175,185,275,285,385,685}020a0, the set with the least complete-traversal charge of entry 0bc5f130. Under this premise the charged preprocessing builds the fixed instance whose filter, budgets, cost and rate proof.md analyses; with these values the search succeeds with probability at least 0.39 under H1' and H4' (proof.md 10.4), so SEL followed by the search needs all three heuristics. Not part of the premise: the cost of SEL, below 2^62.946 operations (below 2^54.198 units; preprocessing_log2 55) by construction whatever the runs return, since every run halts at its cap and every loop has a stated range, and charged in full in time_log2; and the properties of the returned values that the search uses, which proof.md checks exactly for the stated values. Declared, not proved.
heuristics.scope: What SEL returns, not its cost or memory: the three steps of proof.md Section 12 as written, with the instance of each logged run made by the participant's generator, the solver kissat run with the logged seed under a cap of 2^56 operations, the participant's integer counter under a cap of 2^52 (a part of 2^192 or more counts as a capped run), ties broken by the order of the log (step 2) and by increasing mask (step 3), and operations counted as in proof.md Section 11, 430 to the unit. The properties that the search uses of the returned values lie outside the premise; proof.md checks each for the stated values, however they were found: Fact P (3.2), Lemma Q, Theorem C (iii) and (iv), the table of 10.1 with the program of Section 17, the certificate of the filter for S (Section 8) and the verifier of the guards (9.9).
heuristics.extrapolation: From the participant's records, described in proof.md Section 12 (participant records, untrusted by the harness; the generator, the solver log and the counter are not in the package): the solver log, in which the run for lengths 55 and 63 with bound 104 and seed 506 found these six constants after 4,770 seconds, with a solution of class 830303cf and beta 18b0e098; an exact integer recount, by the participant's counter on the whole class of each instance, of all 65 distinct instances that the runs of the log returned with a model, in which these constants have the part 71,698,432, the largest, and the next 13,107,200 (a strict maximum, 5.47 times the next), every model replayed on 32-bit words; the solver and the counter being deterministic for given inputs; every logged run stopped within 9,010.5 seconds on one processor core and every recount within 320 seconds, so that under the stated bridge of at most 2^42 charged operations a second on one core every run used fewer than 2^55.14 operations, below its cap of 2^56, and every recount fewer than 2^50.33, below 2^52; and, for S, GPT Sol's exact integer comparison of all 16,383 nonempty outcome sets under the complete-traversal charge (answers AW 4 and AX 1.2), with a helper agent of the participant finding the same S for the charge with the cap 56,096. Exact checks in proof.md of the returned values, none of which depends on how the values were found: by proof, Fact P (C3 gives equal d and b outputs for W4 and W4'), Lemma Q (the class of eta = 830303cf has exactly 524,288 members) and Theorem C (iv) (c1 gives the difference beta* = 18b0e098 exactly when c1 AND 0e09818b = 02008000, the 2^21 words of Q*); by exact counts printed with their program or certificate (participant runs, reproducible from the text), the table of 10.1 and the program of Section 17 (the fourteen outcomes of beta* on the class, all with eps = 6e21be55; the part 71,698,432 of beta* that step 2 compares, asserted by the program; 67,633,152 = 1,032 * 2^16 for the six of S), the certificate of the filter for S (pi = 279,070,422,111 / 2^48) and the verifier of 9.9 (the guards of the solver in all eight phases).
heuristics.limitations: The full capped selection was not replayed: SEL as written, with its operation caps, has not been run end to end by the participant or by the organizer, and the records are of historical runs, not of a replay with caps. The bridge from wall-clock time to charged operations (at most 2^42 a second on one core, from the clock, the issue width and at most 64 operations per executed instruction) is stated and not proved, so it is not proved that the logged runs stayed within the caps of 2^56 and 2^52. The log does not fix every instance: some runs excluded pairs that runs finished before them had found, so their instances depend on the order in which runs finished, and 32 runs were stopped from outside without a recorded cause. The generator, the solver log and the counter are not in the package, and the organizer-run experiments do not run SEL. That these values have the largest part among the 65 recounted instances rests on the recount; Section 17 recomputes only their own part. Step 3 applies the complete-traversal charge of entry 0bc5f130 as a fixed rule; whether S is also the least set under the one-path charge of proof.md Section 11 has not been compared. If a record were wrong, SEL could return other values or none; its cost would stay within the bound, but the charged preprocessing would not build the instance that proof.md analyses, and these values would stand as advice whose cost of construction is not justified.
